forces.title: Dutch road freight faces double-digit cost inflation
forces.description: Dutch road freight operators face severe cost pressure from higher wages, a 30% surge in diesel prices due to the Iran war, and the introduction of new truck charges. Labour costs account for roughly half of total operating costs, with collective agreements and workforce aging pushing them up. Fuel surcharges help, but the speed of increase creates temporary lags affecting profitability. The new truck charging scheme adds 7-8% to total transport costs, forcing operators to focus on tight margin management and rapid pricing adjustments to prevent liquidity pressures, testing financial resilience.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: Infrastructure maintenance backlogs causing detours and inefficiencies
forces.description: The Netherlands faces a growing challenge from infrastructure maintenance backlogs, estimated at €34.5 billion through 2038. Ageing infrastructure, particularly bridges from the 1960s and 1970s, requires major maintenance or replacement, leading to unexpected closures and restrictions for heavy freight transport. These disruptions force detours, increasing operating costs and reducing efficiency for transport companies. While the government committed an additional €1.5 billion from 2027, this is insufficient, implying more frequent bottlenecks and a decline in the country's reputation for world-class infrastructure, impacting road freight operations.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: European road freight contract rates rising, offsetting costs
forces.description: European road freight contract rates have shown a relatively strong increase, with an average rise of around 9% during the second quarter. This upward trend in rates is broadly sufficient to offset the rapid rise in operating costs, including wages, diesel prices, and new truck charges, helping transport operators maintain profitability. The ability to pass on costs contractually is crucial for financial resilience in a high-inflation environment. However, the temporary lag in cost pass-through for sudden fuel price surges still impacts short-term margins, requiring agile pricing strategies.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: Geopolitical conflict causing diesel price surge, impacting profitability
forces.description: The conflict involving Iran has pushed diesel prices in Europe around 30% higher than 2025 levels, significantly impacting road transport operators. Europe's heavy dependence on diesel imports and tight refining capacity suggest these elevated prices are likely to persist. While fuel surcharges are typically passed on contractually, the rapid speed of the increase has created a temporary lag in cost recovery, affecting profitability. This geopolitical risk translates into a direct and substantial headwind for road freight, increasing financial pressure and necessitating agile cost management strategies.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: Dutch truck charge accelerates zero-emission freight transition
forces.description: The introduction of the Dutch truck charging scheme in July 2026 significantly increases operating costs for road freight transport. However, the revenues generated from this scheme are being recycled into sustainability investments within the sector. This creates a dual effect: it adds immediate financial pressure on operators but also improves the business case for electric trucks. This structural change is expected to accelerate the transition towards zero-emission freight transport, aligning the sector with climate objectives and driving long-term fleet modernization.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: Regulation, digitalization, AI drive industry consolidation
forces.description: New sustainability regulations, increasing digitalization, and the growing adoption of artificial intelligence are collectively driving up investment requirements and demand for specialist expertise across the Dutch transport sector. This environment creates a competitive advantage for larger transport operators who have greater capacity to invest in ICT systems, fleet electrification, and specialized personnel. Consequently, consolidation through merger and acquisition activity is expected to continue, as smaller firms without succession plans or facing major investment hurdles opt to sell, reshaping the industry landscape.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: Resilient global trade and longer shipping routes boost maritime
forces.description: Global goods trade continues to grow, unexpectedly remaining near 5% during the first half of 2026, largely driven by China's export expansion. Despite much of this trade bypassing European ports, globally active Dutch shipping companies benefit from the overall resilience. Disruptions in key waterways like the Red Sea, Black Sea, Strait of Hormuz, and Panama Canal are maintaining longer sailing distances. This directly supports demand for shipping services and freight rates, providing a significant tailwind for the Shipping & Maritime sector and related logistics providers.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Dutch public transport faces infrastructure, price headwinds
forces.description: Despite a faster-than-anticipated recovery in public transport usage in the Netherlands, the sector faces ongoing headwinds. Infrastructure projects are causing disruptions, and a cumulative 13% rise in ticket prices since early 2025 creates pressure on passenger volumes. Although rail punctuality has improved, the overall operating environment remains challenging. These factors contribute to financial pressure for public transit operators, necessitating careful management of service levels and pricing strategies to maintain ridership amidst persistent cost and operational complexities.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Post-pandemic travel patterns shift, impacting public transit demand
forces.description: Travel patterns in the Netherlands have permanently changed since the pandemic, with demand spread more evenly across the week. This structural shift impacts the predictability and profitability of traditional public transport services. While overall usage has recovered, regional public transport continues to lag due to budget reductions, route cancellations, and reduced frequencies. This necessitates an adaptation in service planning and resource allocation for road, ground, and public transit operators, who must adjust to new demand profiles and potentially more dispersed peak travel times to optimize operations and revenue streams.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Schiphol's capacity constraints and high fuel costs limit airline growth
forces.description: Schiphol Airport faces significant limitations for growth, operating near its practical capacity limit. This, combined with elevated jet fuel costs, contributes to fewer flights and substantial increases in airfares (around 7.5% higher in summer 2026). Europe's dependence on imported jet fuel and high refining margins suggest fuel costs will remain elevated. These factors present a considerable headwind for airlines operating at Schiphol, restricting their ability to expand flight volumes and forcing continuous pressure to raise fares, potentially impacting demand elasticity.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Stricter aviation sustainability policies increase operational costs
forces.description: Airlines in Europe face additional upward pressure on operational costs due to stricter sustainability policies. These include the full phase-out of free emissions allowances for intra-European flights, increasing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) requirements, and the planned distance-based aviation tax from 2027 (potentially rising to almost €60 from a flat €30). These regulatory changes contribute to higher operating expenses for airlines, forcing them to raise fares. The policies represent a significant headwind, demanding investment in greener fuels and efficiency improvements, ultimately impacting profitability and competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Logistics providers benefit from supply chain volatility and outsourcing
forces.description: Logistics service providers are outperforming the broader transport sector, driven by heightened volatility in global trade and increased outsourcing of supply chain activities. Growing uncertainty has strengthened their strategic role, with rising demand for reliability, speed, and resilience, especially for high-value products. This environment, coupled with elevated air and ocean freight rates, creates solid opportunities. Logistics providers leverage their expertise in warehousing, inventory management, and supply chain management to deliver value, mitigating risks for clients and securing robust business in complex global trading conditions.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Rotterdam port capacity constraints cause congestion
forces.description: Container throughput in the Port of Rotterdam remained broadly stable in the first half of 2026, but empty-container volumes surged, reflecting widening trade imbalances between Europe and Asia. This increase in empty container movements creates significant congestion and operational inefficiencies within the port. Terminal capacity constraints remain a bottleneck for both shipping companies and freight logistics. While planned expansions on Maasvlakte 2 should provide some relief from 2027, the current situation represents a persistent headwind, impacting port efficiency and turnaround times for maritime transport and logistics operations.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Inland shipping low water levels risk modal shift to road
forces.description: Exceptionally low water levels in the Netherlands have once again restricted inland shipping capacity, leading to loading limitations and tight vessel availability, which has pushed freight rates higher. While financially strong for inland operators in the short term, recurring disruptions are problematic. They risk encouraging shippers to shift freight to road transport, undermining long-term modal shift ambitions towards more sustainable inland waterway transport. This presents a key risk of structural shift away from maritime transport for inland routes if water level issues persist, impacting environmental targets and infrastructure planning.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: EU parcel levy reduces international parcel demand
forces.description: The introduction of the €3 European parcel levy has notably impacted demand for international parcels, particularly shipments linked to Chinese online platforms, leading to a marked decline in Chinese parcel volumes during summer 2026. This headwind for parcel logistics is causing a shift in traffic towards consolidated shipments and maritime transport, followed by European fulfilment-centre distribution. The levy represents a regulatory barrier that alters trade flows and business models for freight, logistics & supply chain companies, requiring adaptation to new operational strategies and potentially influencing consumer purchasing habits for cross-border e-commerce.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Labour shortages remain significant challenge for Dutch T&L
forces.description: Labour availability continues to be one of the biggest challenges for the Dutch transport and logistics sector. Although vacancy rates have eased slightly, they remain well above pre-pandemic levels. Shortages persist for critical roles such as drivers, conductors, and warehouse workers, with increasing scarcity of maintenance technicians and IT specialists. Ageing demographics, limited new worker inflows, and elevated sickness absence constrain the labour supply. This represents a significant headwind, impacting operational capacity, driving up wage costs, and hindering growth potential across airlines, road freight, rail, and logistics services.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Agentic AI reduces coordination tax in logistics workflows
forces.description: Agentic AI systems are fundamentally reshaping business workflows by automating verification, reconciliation, and routing at interfaces, significantly reducing the 'coordination tax'. This technology allows for machine-speed judgment across process boundaries, collapsing latency from days to hours or minutes. For freight, logistics & supply chain, this means potential tenfold improvements in planning clock speed, 80% touchless planning, and significantly faster reaction times to supply shocks and demand opportunities. This structural change offers substantial profit impact by streamlining operations and enabling human workers to focus on high-value, exception-based decisions rather than routine coordination.
forces.source_title: Cutting the ‘coordination tax’: How agentic AI can reshape workflows

forces.title: European AI startups build tailored, compliance-ready transport solutions
forces.description: European AI startups are developing deeply tailored, compliance-ready solutions for complex industries like transport, mobility, and logistics. Leveraging Europe's heterogeneous markets and stringent regulatory environment (e.g., GDPR, EU AI Act), these companies embed AI products deep into enterprise systems, understanding live operational context and executing permitted actions. This approach creates valuable enterprise moats, including higher switching costs and faster procurement in regulated industries. This structural change positions European startups to deliver specialized, integrated AI applications that genuinely change how work is done in the transport sector.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Upskilling workforce for AI fluency boosts T&L competitiveness
forces.description: The increasing demand for AI fluency, combined with a focus on workforce upskilling and workflow redesign, is becoming critical for building lean and competitive businesses in Europe's transport and logistics sector. Structured Gen AI training can significantly accelerate tasks like coding, while peer-driven learning models efficiently institutionalize adoption. This upside driver enables companies to overcome capital and labor cost constraints, improving operational efficiency and allowing teams to adapt rapidly to evolving technological landscapes. A CEO- and board-level commitment is essential to inspire and drive this organization-wide transformation.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Chinese OEMs challenge European truck market with cost/speed advantage
forces.description: Chinese OEMs are building an inevitable presence in the European truck market, fueled by large domestic manufacturing capacity and higher-margin export sales. They offer a structural cost advantage of 30-40% (even with local EU production) and product development cycles that are twice as fast (22-28 months vs. 40-48 months). This structural change intensifies competition for European road freight operators, as Chinese entrants offer more competitive total cost of ownership (TCO) and innovative features like battery-swapping ecosystems and AI-native smart cockpits, potentially capturing significant market share by 2035.
forces.source_title: Competing against Chinese innovation speed in European trucking

forces.title: European truck OEMs face CO2 penalties, rising competition
forces.description: European truck manufacturers are under increasing pressure from potential CO2 penalties if they fail to meet regulatory targets for zero-emission (ZE) vehicle adoption. This is compounded by growing competition from new entrants, particularly Chinese OEMs, who are entering European markets with cost and learning-curve advantages in electric and hydrogen-powered trucks. The slow rate of ZE truck adoption (below 5% in 2025) exposes European OEMs to significant economic costs and challenges their technology and market leadership. This represents a strong headwind impacting future profitability and market share.
forces.source_title: Zero-emission trucks: Accelerating Europe’s transition

forces.title: New entrants challenge European ZE truck market leadership
forces.description: The European ZE truck market is seeing new entrants, primarily Chinese OEMs, challenging established leadership by entering with cost and learning-curve advantages. These players have already launched electric and hydrogen-powered trucks across European markets. This structural change introduces significant competition, requiring European OEMs and road freight operators to accelerate their transition to zero-emission vehicles. The ability of these new entrants to build scale elsewhere and leverage lower manufacturing costs creates pressure on pricing and market share, necessitating a strategic response from incumbents.
forces.source_title: Zero-emission trucks: Accelerating Europe’s transition

forces.title: Vehicle dimensions directive revision to boost ZE truck viability
forces.description: The ongoing revision of the European Vehicle Dimensions directive is a potential tailwind for the adoption of zero-emission (ZE) trucks. By allowing higher gross vehicle weights, this revision could largely address the operational disadvantages imposed by the additional weight of batteries and hydrogen storage vessels. This regulatory adaptation would improve the economic feasibility and practical utility of ZE trucks for road freight operators, making them more competitive against traditional diesel vehicles. It removes a key barrier, encouraging greater investment and uptake of greener transport solutions.
forces.source_title: Zero-emission trucks: Accelerating Europe’s transition

forces.title: ZE truck TCO variability challenges broad adoption
forces.description: Zero-emission (ZE) trucks present a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) advantage for about 30% of the truck market, but their attractiveness varies significantly by use case and country. While 20% of European road freight operates in countries with consistent ZE truck TCO advantages, cross-border use cases are fragile due to differences in tolling, taxation, energy prices, and charging availability. This structural challenge requires either a 10-20% decline in up-front costs or adoption of differentiated road tolls by more EU member states to increase market share and overcome TCO variability for road freight operators.
forces.source_title: Zero-emission trucks: Accelerating Europe’s transition

forces.title: Cross-border factors erode ZE truck TCO advantage
forces.description: Differences in tolling, taxation, energy prices, charging availability, and public-charging tariffs across EU member states can quickly erode the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) advantage of zero-emission (ZE) trucks, particularly for open-network long-haul operations. This presents a key risk for road freight operators seeking to transition to ZE fleets, as the economic benefits become unpredictable and complex across borders. Without greater harmonization of these factors, the financial viability of cross-border ZE trucking remains precarious, hindering widespread adoption and creating operational inefficiencies for carriers.
forces.source_title: Zero-emission trucks: Accelerating Europe’s transition

forces.title: Customer hesitation impacts AV truck adoption
forces.description: Customer hesitation is a significant barrier to the adoption of autonomous trucks, with only 36% of fleet buyers expressing readiness in 2026. Concerns cited include unclear legal liability, lack of regulations, and limited exposure to the technology. A third of buyers also believe their fleets rarely operate in situations benefiting from autonomous driving. This key risk requires OEMs and technology providers to demonstrate reliability through extensive pilot programs and transparent data sharing to build trust and increase market interest for autonomous road freight services.

forces.title: AV trucks shift value to software, remote services
forces.description: Autonomous heavy-duty trucks are poised to fundamentally shift the industry's focus from hardware sales to high-margin software deployed in AVs, remote teleoperations, and predictive maintenance services. This represents a significant structural change for road freight operators, creating new value pools and business models beyond traditional vehicle ownership. The entire value of AV truck deployment in Europe could reach €100 billion by 2035, emphasizing the growing importance of technology and service-oriented offerings over pure vehicle sales, necessitating a strategic reorientation for industry players.

forces.title: UN ECE WP.29 regulations pave way for AV scale-up
forces.description: The upcoming United Nations Economic Commission for Europe WP.29 regulations are an upside driver for autonomous vehicle (AV) adoption, as they introduce the first global framework for fully autonomous driving. This harmonization of standards will help pave the way for a major European scale-up of AV trucks and buses after 2030. These regulations provide much-needed legal certainty and a consistent operating environment, reducing risks and facilitating investments in AV technology, ultimately supporting the wider commercial deployment and integration of autonomous road freight and public transit services.

forces.title: Severe driver shortages necessitate autonomous buses
forces.description: Europe faces severe labor shortages in its public transit sector, with Germany alone projected to have a deficit of 80,000 bus drivers by 2030. This critical shortage is a major headwind for public bus operators, driving autonomous buses (ABs) to emerge as an economic necessity. While a challenge for traditional operations, it acts as a tailwind for AV technology adoption, projected to capture 60% of the city bus market by 2045. This force pushes the sector towards innovative solutions to maintain service levels and address escalating operational costs.

forces.title: Autonomous tech enables smaller, more flexible buses
forces.description: Autonomous technology is creating a structural shift in urban mobility by making smaller buses economically viable for mass transit. This allows cities to deploy smaller vehicles at higher frequencies and launch new routes despite lower demand, expanding service reach and efficiency. Smaller form factors are expected to account for about 65% of the market by 2045. This change enables public transit operators to transition service portfolios from pure hardware sales towards 'as-a-service' offerings, redefining vehicle types, customer segments, and service models in the road, ground, and public transit sector.

forces.title: Financial services critical for ZEV leasing and TCO viability
forces.description: The financial services sector is becoming crucial for the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) transition in trucking, driven by the higher value of ZEV assets and increased finance/leasing penetration. Financial service players can become key orchestrators of downstream value creation by absorbing residual-value uncertainty and translating improved Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) into bankable, life cycle–integrated contracts. This structural change is vital for ZEV scalability, as residual-value uncertainty is a major obstacle to ZEV leasing. Success depends on making high-value ZEV assets economically viable for road freight operators.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Residual-value uncertainty impedes ZEV leasing scale
forces.description: Residual-value uncertainty is identified as the biggest obstacle to scaling zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) leasing in the European trucking industry. This risk makes it challenging for financial services players and fleet operators to accurately price and manage the long-term asset value of ZEVs, despite their potential Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) advantages. Overcoming this requires robust financial models and risk mitigation strategies to encourage wider adoption of ZEVs in road freight. Without clear residual value projections, the shift to electric and hydrogen trucks through leasing models will remain constrained.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Electrification rapidly transforms MHDT aftermarket
forces.description: Electrification is swiftly transforming the medium- and heavy-duty truck (MHDT) aftermarket in Europe, becoming the primary source of growth after 2030. Sales of new zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) are expected to account for around 46% of the EU HDT market by 2035, with associated aftermarket revenue expanding at a 40-50% CAGR through 2035. This structural change requires significant investment in staff and training for high-voltage diagnostics and battery-health monitoring. OEMs and service providers must adapt their capabilities ahead of the curve to capitalize on this shift from traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) servicing.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Private investment crucial for ZE truck charging infrastructure
forces.description: To accelerate the zero-emission (ZE) truck transition, unlocking €12 billion in private investment by 2030 is crucial for developing charging infrastructure. This investment is needed to close the gap between current infrastructure and the 15,000-20,000 public fast-charging points and 200,000 fleet hub/depot points required by 2030. Systematic derisking, simplified grid access, and faster permitting are key enablers. This represents a significant upside driver, as adequate infrastructure will unlock the full potential of ZE trucks and prevent long-term lock-in of emission levels for road freight operators.
forces.source_title: Competing in the fast lane—the future of Europe’s truck industry

forces.title: High customer willingness to switch to ZE trucks
forces.description: A significant upside driver for the zero-emission (ZE) truck market is high customer willingness to switch, with 60% of European fleet operators ready to adopt ZE trucks at Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) parity, and up to 80% willing if TCO is 10% lower than comparable diesel vehicles. This strong market interest, driven by reduced CO2 emissions, regulatory incentives, and lower operating costs, indicates that economic attractiveness is key to accelerating adoption. It provides a clear path for OEMs and service providers to drive demand by focusing on TCO optimization and attractive upfront costs for road freight operators.
forces.source_title: Zero-emission trucks: Accelerating Europe’s transition

forces.title: Chinese OEM upfront cost advantage challenges European ZE trucks
forces.description: The attractive up-front costs offered by Chinese OEMs in the zero-emission (ZE) truck market pose a significant headwind for European competitors. This cost advantage allows Chinese brands to gain a competitive foothold, appealing to European fleet operators who prioritize Total Cost of Ownership (TCO). While European OEMs offer advanced ZE vehicles, the pricing pressure from Chinese entrants necessitates rigorous cost efficiency and faster time-to-market strategies. This challenges European manufacturers and ultimately impacts the purchasing decisions of road freight operators, potentially accelerating the shift to non-European suppliers.
forces.source_title: Zero-emission trucks: Accelerating Europe’s transition

forces.title: Customer demand shifts to bundled transport service packages
forces.description: Customer expectations in the trucking industry are undergoing a structural shift towards bundled packages that include vehicle provision, fleet management, remote-operations support, charging, predictive maintenance, and uptime guarantees, rather than discrete transactions. This change is driven by the increasing complexity of zero-emission vehicles and the need for integrated solutions to manage their life cycle and operations. While positive for players that can monetize these comprehensive services, it poses a genuine structural threat to standalone revenue lines like crash repair, forcing a reorientation of business models for road freight operators and service providers.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Chinese OEMs' price advantage creates market share scenarios
forces.description: The European truck market faces a key risk from Chinese OEMs, whose significant price advantage (15-40% lower) could lead to two disruptive scenarios. In one, they gain a competitive, low double-digit share. In a more radical shift, an accelerated green transition and deep local footprint propel them to robust double-digit market leadership. This pricing strategy, enabled by structural cost advantages and innovative business models (e.g., bundling energy solutions), is testing European brand loyalty and poses a severe threat to incumbent road freight operators, necessitating a rapid strategic response.
forces.source_title: Competing against Chinese innovation speed in European trucking

forces.title: Europe-led battery value chain and hydrogen roadmap vital
forces.description: Developing a Europe-led battery value chain and a clear roadmap towards the use of hydrogen are critical enablers for maintaining long-term competitiveness in the trucking industry. Currently, Europe accounts for less than 10% of global battery-cell production capacity. Strengthening strategic independence in key components and energy sources is a significant upside driver. This proactive approach will help regain technology leadership, reduce reliance on external suppliers (like China), and ensure a stable, cost-effective supply for the burgeoning zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) market for road freight operators.
forces.source_title: Competing in the fast lane—the future of Europe’s truck industry

forces.title: Favorable regulatory environment and ecosystem cooperation fosters growth
forces.description: Establishing a transparent and predictable regulatory environment, coupled with greater cooperation across the trucking ecosystem, are crucial upside drivers for the industry. Offtake guarantees or backstops for initial investments can help derisk the significant capital required for the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) transition. Once established, ZEV trucks and infrastructure offer attractive economics, making growth self-sustaining. This collaborative framework, involving infrastructure operators, battery industry players, technology providers, regulatory bodies, and policymakers, creates the stability and certainty needed for multiyear investments, benefiting all segments of the transport and logistics sector.
forces.source_title: Competing in the fast lane—the future of Europe’s truck industry

viewpoints.title: B2B agentic commerce to drive future logistics procurement automation
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights B2B agentic commerce as among the least commercially deployed but poised for significant advancement by 2030. This shift implies automation of sourcing, evaluating bids, negotiating parameters, and executing settlement against institutional criteria. For logistics, this represents a cautious positive outlook on future efficiency gains and reduced transactional friction, potentially streamlining freight procurement and supply chain management processes. This structural evolution in B2B transactions could reshape how transportation and logistics services are bought and sold, demanding adaptation from service providers.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Dutch road freight cautiously recovers despite significant cost pressures
viewpoints.description: ING Think projects a cautious recovery for Dutch road freight transport, with volumes expected to grow by around 1% in 2026 and 1.5% in 2027. Despite improving market conditions and increasing European contract rates, operators face mounting cost pressure from higher wages, a 30% diesel price surge, and new truck charges. This indicates a challenging environment where rising revenues are largely offset by escalating operational costs, keeping margins under significant pressure. Financial resilience will be tested, driving a focus on cost control and rapid pricing adjustments.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

viewpoints.title: Dutch transport and logistics to see moderate growth into 2027
viewpoints.description: The Dutch transport and logistics sector is forecast by ING Think to achieve moderate growth of around 1% in 2026 and 1.5% in 2027. This growth is supported by resilient global trade, consumer demand, and strong performance in aviation and maritime shipping, despite initial expectations of a slowdown. However, the sector is also grappling with significant headwinds including rising costs, geopolitical uncertainties, and climate-related disruptions. The positive outlook is tempered by the need for strong pricing power and strategic adaptation to navigate increasing volatility and investment requirements across subsectors.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Dutch passenger transport expected to perform especially well
viewpoints.description: ING Think anticipates strong performance in Dutch passenger transport, driven by a faster-than-expected recovery in public transport usage. This rebound is attributed to factors like a robust spring season and government-supported summer travel subscription initiatives, which temporarily pushed usage above pre-pandemic levels. While regional transport lags due to budget cuts and reduced frequencies, the overall recovery trajectory for public transport is seen as structurally positive. This suggests a shift in commuting and travel patterns that benefits public transit operators.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Logistics service providers benefit from volatile global trading environment
viewpoints.description: Logistics service providers are expected to continue outperforming the broader transport sector, according to ING Think. The increasing volatility in global trade, coupled with a trend towards outsourcing supply chain activities, has significantly strengthened their strategic importance. Demand for reliability, speed, and enhanced supply chain resilience, particularly for high-value products, is growing. This environment, alongside elevated air and ocean freight rates, creates solid opportunities for many logistics providers, allowing them to leverage their expertise in warehousing, inventory management, and supply chain management for sustained growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Dutch parcel delivery market matures, slowing from rapid growth
viewpoints.description: ING Think indicates that the Dutch parcel logistics market is entering a more mature phase after years of rapid expansion. Growth is decelerating as e-commerce penetration increases and consumers increasingly utilize parcel lockers, collection points, and store-based fulfillment options. International parcels, particularly from Chinese online platforms, a major past growth driver, are now seeing reduced demand due to the introduction of a European parcel levy. This implies a shift towards consolidated shipments and maritime transport, with European fulfillment centers gaining importance.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Schiphol's future growth hinges on larger aircraft and higher load factors
viewpoints.description: ING Think notes that Schiphol Airport is operating close to its practical capacity limit of approximately 478,000 flights annually. Despite a quick recovery in demand post-Middle East conflict, future growth for airline operators at Schiphol will depend primarily on the deployment of larger aircraft and achieving higher load factors. Government plans for Lelystad Airport aim to relieve pressure by shifting European flights, but implementation remains uncertain. This outlook presents a cautious negative view for airlines relying on Schiphol for expansion, emphasizing efficiency over volume growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Larger transport operators gain competitive edge, driving consolidation
viewpoints.description: ING Think asserts that larger transport operators are gaining a competitive advantage in the current environment, driven by increased investment requirements for ICT systems, fleet electrification, and specialized personnel. Their scale allows them to spread overhead costs more effectively, fostering continued consolidation across the transport sector. This suggests a positive outlook for established, larger players who are better equipped to meet new sustainability regulations, digitalisation mandates, and AI adoption. Smaller firms, often lacking these capacities, are increasingly opting to sell, contributing to market restructuring.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

viewpoints.title: Air cargo thriving amid global trade uncertainty and supply chain disruptions
viewpoints.description: ING Think highlights that air freight remains a highly attractive option when speed and reliability are paramount, thriving amidst ongoing global trade uncertainty and supply chain disruptions. The Asia region, particularly China, has become an increasingly significant source for Dutch air cargo imports, reflecting its growing role in global trade. Despite a slowdown in Chinese parcel volumes, the overall demand for air freight continues to be supported by the critical need for flexibility and resilience in supply chains. This presents a positive outlook for air cargo operators.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

viewpoints.title: Agentic AI to revolutionize workflows by eliminating coordination tax
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that agentic AI is poised to fundamentally reshape workflows by automating verification, reconciliation, and routing at interfaces, drastically reducing the 'coordination tax'. This technology, unlike previous automation, possesses the judgment to act across process boundaries, collapsing latency from days to minutes. For logistics and supply chain management, this implies a highly positive outlook for efficiency gains, with planning clock speed improving tenfold and routine decisions becoming touchless. It enables human planners to focus on high-value anomalies rather than routine coordination, leading to substantial profit impact.
viewpoints.source_title: Cutting the ‘coordination tax’: How agentic AI can reshape workflows

viewpoints.title: Europe's AI edge emerging in vertical transport, mobility, logistics applications
viewpoints.description: McKinsey identifies 'transport, mobility, and logistics' as a key vertical industry attracting substantial AI investment in Europe. This sector is exhibiting emerging strength in AI applications, driven by deeply entrenched incumbents, affiliated research, and regulatory rigor. European startups are leveraging these 'structural assets' to build specialized, compliance-ready solutions. The report suggests a positive outlook for Europe gaining a competitive edge by developing adaptable, deeply tailored software embedded directly into enterprise systems, capitalizing on complex localized needs and stringent regulatory environments like GDPR and the EU AI Act.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Slow ZE truck adoption necessitates step change for decarbonization targets
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that new registrations of zero-emission (ZE) trucks remained below 5% as of 2025, despite European manufacturers releasing many models. This slow adoption rate underscores an urgent need for a step change to accelerate decarbonization and avoid rising economic costs, including potential CO2 penalties for OEMs. The outlook is cautiously negative, emphasizing that delays lock in emission levels and expose the European industry to competition from new entrants with cost and learning-curve advantages. Greater economic attractiveness and infrastructure boost are crucial for success.

viewpoints.title: Autonomous trucks and buses to fundamentally transform transport sectors
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects that autonomous vehicles (AVs), particularly trucks and buses, are set to fundamentally change the road freight and urban mobility sectors. These technologies will create lucrative new profit pools, shifting value from hardware sales to high-margin software, remote teleoperations, and predictive maintenance services. This represents a highly positive structural change for transport operators. While Europe currently trails the US and China in AV trucking, upcoming UN regulations are expected to pave the way for a major European scale-up after 2030, driven by economic necessity and labor shortages.
viewpoints.source_title: Mastering autonomous truck technology in Europe

viewpoints.title: Financial services key orchestrator for downstream value in trucking life cycle
viewpoints.description: McKinsey projects that financial service players will become critical orchestrators of downstream value creation in the trucking industry. This involves controlling the commercial life cycle through financing, contracts, risk transfer, residual value management, and asset steering, especially for high-value Zero-Emission Vehicles (ZEVs). Their role extends to maintaining continuous customer interfaces, fostering retention, and enabling bundled services. This presents a positive view for the sector, as financial services make ZEV assets economically viable, absorb residual value uncertainty, and translate improved Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) into integrated contracts, which are crucial for customer adoption.
viewpoints.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

viewpoints.title: European OEMs must adapt strategy against rising Chinese trucking competition
viewpoints.description: McKinsey warns that Europe's truck market, despite domestic OEMs holding over 90% share, faces significant disruption from Chinese competitors. Chinese OEMs, having doubled global market share in five years and holding substantial shares in electric buses and forklifts, are accelerating exports to Europe. Their structural cost advantage (30-40%) and faster development cycles (2x) enable competitive pricing and innovative offerings. This necessitates a strategic shift for European OEMs to defend their dominant position, focusing on cost efficiency, customer centricity, and integrated energy solutions to counter this growing threat.
viewpoints.source_title: Competing against Chinese innovation speed in European trucking
